- id: f001
  description: 'MECHANISM PROFILE — context-mismatched spinlock (missing bottom-half disable). UNTRUSTED SOURCE: not attacker-supplied data but attacker-influenced concurrency triggers — any packet/event that executes the device''s softirq-context callback (ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, timer-driven xmit) while a process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/firmware/SME request) holds the same lock on that CPU; local or remote traffic and timer expiry are enough to align both sides. MISSING GUARANTEE: lock-context discipline — a spinlock reachable from softirq/timer context must be acquired with spin_lock_bh()/local_bh_disable() at every process-context site; plain spin_lock() only disables preemption, not bottom halves, so a softirq can run on the same CPU between lock and unlock. UNSAFE USE: process call chain (worker -> driver helper -> hw_tx/enqueue) holds the plain-acquired lock, then a softirq on the same CPU spins forever trying to take that same lock while the holder can never resume — a self-deadlock. CONSEQUENCE: softirq/soft-lockup on one CPU, RCU stall and watchdog splats, device TX stall, repeatable denial of service. The invariant generalizes one level up: a lock shared with a hardirq handler needs irqsave/irq-disable at non-irq sites. Seed (staging ks7010 tx_dev_lock, workqueue xmit path vs xmit callback) is a demonstration only and must never be reported. BRANCHES: branch1=xmit-softirq-lock: in net/wireless/staging drivers, find lock objects taken with plain spin_lock in process/workqueue-context helpers (hw-tx, request, firmware, ioctl paths) that are also acquired in code reachable from ndo_start_xmit or TX-completion callbacks that can run under NET_TX/NET_RX softirq — the exact seed shape; branch2=timer-dwork-softirq-lock: find locks acquired inside timer_list, hrtimer, or delayed_work callback bodies (timer softirq context) that are also taken with plain spin_lock from process-context paths (workers, ioctls, open/close, config), yielding softirq-vs-holder deadlock; branch3=tasklet-napi-softirq-lock: find locks shared between process-context code and tasklet_schedule''d functions or NAPI poll / other NET softirq callbacks where the process side uses plain spin_lock instead of spin_lock_bh (excluding xmit and timer callbacks covered by branches 1-2); branch4=hardirq-shared-lock: the interrupt-level analog of the same invariant — locks acquired inside hardirq handlers (request_irq / non-threaded part of request_threaded_irq) that are taken with plain spin_lock (no spin_lock_irqsave/irq) in process or softirq context, allowing the hardirq to preempt and spin on a lock the preempted context can never release.'

- id: f001
  description: 'MECHANISM PROFILE — context-mismatched spinlock (missing bottom-half disable). UNTRUSTED SOURCE: not attacker-supplied data but attacker-influenced concurrency triggers — any packet/event that executes the device''s softirq-context callback (ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, timer-driven xmit) while a process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/firmware/SME request) holds the same lock on that CPU; local or remote traffic and timer expiry are enough to align both sides. MISSING GUARANTEE: lock-context discipline — a spinlock reachable from softirq/timer context must be acquired with spin_lock_bh()/local_bh_disable() at every process-context site; plain spin_lock() only disables preemption, not bottom halves, so a softirq can run on the same CPU between lock and unlock. UNSAFE USE: process call chain (worker -> driver helper -> hw_tx/enqueue) holds the plain-acquired lock, then a softirq on the same CPU spins forever trying to take that same lock while the holder can never resume — a self-deadlock. CONSEQUENCE: softirq/soft-lockup on one CPU, RCU stall and watchdog splats, device TX stall, repeatable denial of service. The invariant generalizes one level up: a lock shared with a hardirq handler needs irqsave/irq-disable at non-irq sites. Seed (staging ks7010 tx_dev_lock, workqueue xmit path vs xmit callback) is a demonstration only and must never be reported.     """Find definition of `name` and return its body text (or None)."""
    # candidate definitions: at line start, some modifiers, name( ... ) then {

        i = m.end()  # after name(
        depth = 1
        j = i
        while j < len(text) and depth > 0:
            c = text[j]
            if c == '(': depth += 1
            elif c == ')': depth -= 1
            j += 1
        # now text[j-1] == ')'
